headline: Nation Divided As Citizens Start Naming Their Household Appliances After Political Slogans
body:
“My pressure cooker is now officially branded the ‘Anti-National Steamer,’ so every time the whistle blows, I feel like I’m participating in a high-stakes national debate,” said a local accountant while scrubbing a lid.

“I’ve started labeling my ceiling fan the ‘Globalist Wind-Machine,’ and honestly, it keeps the room quite chilly, though the debates in my living room have become entirely unbearable,” remarked a college student living in a hostel.

“My neighbor tried to tell me that my refrigerator is a ‘Dimagi Toaster’ because it keeps the milk too cold, and now we haven’t spoken since last Tuesday,” noted a neighborhood grocery shopkeeper.

“I find it incredibly liberating to just label my toaster a ‘Policy Reformer’ and be done with it; at least it actually manages to brown the bread, unlike the real thing,” admitted a retired software engineer.

“The real tragedy is that my vacuum cleaner is named after a major political shift, and it’s started refusing to pick up dust from any corner that doesn't align with its core ideology,” said a local resident while sighing at a mess.
caption: From kitchen appliances to ceiling fans, everything is getting a political makeover. Are you picking sides, or just waiting for the toast to pop? #Politics #HomeDecor #Satire (satire)
igHook: What’s the most ridiculous name you’ve given an appliance in your house?
imagePrompt: A close-up shot of a modern kitchen appliance with a handwritten masking tape label stuck on it in a residential kitchen setting.

sourceHeadline.title: CJP slams PM Modi for reviving ‘Dimagi Naxal’ remark at SRCC: ‘Give hope, not stupid labels’ | India News

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 0 provides the most grounded and absurd premise, successfully turning a common social tension (political division) into a domestic ritual. It feels fresh compared to the deluge of 'government mandates policy' stories, offering a warmer, more relatable brand of humor centered on kitchen appliances rather than just another layer of cold bureaucracy.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses anonymous, generic archetypes to satirize political polarization without targeting specific real individuals, religious groups, or castes. The image prompt is generic and avoids sensitive content or real-world branding.
